title: Cannabis Aphid: Biology, Evidence & Threshold Uncertainty

content.overview: Cannabis aphid is a Cannabis-associated piercing-sucking insect that can occur on leaves, stems and reproductive growth. Specialist scouting uses direct aphid evidence, honeydew, cast skins, plant response and distribution while avoiding unsupported economic or action thresholds.

vocabulary.definition: Phorodon cannabis, a piercing-sucking aphid associated with Cannabis and hemp.
Sugar-rich liquid excreted by aphids and some other sap-feeding insects that can coat plant surfaces.
A shed exoskeleton left after an arthropod molts; aphid cast skins can support identification and population evidence.

sections.title: Use organism and feeding evidence together
sections.body: Cannabis aphids feed on plant fluids and may occur on leaves, stems and flowering tissues. Mixed life stages, cast skins and honeydew can provide direct evidence that strengthens the diagnosis beyond nonspecific yellowing, wilting or reduced vigor.

sections.title: Population significance depends on context
sections.body: The cited hemp extension literature notes that research-based action thresholds were not established in that production context. Do not turn a count into a universal treatment trigger. Record sampling effort, crop stage, affected scope, trend, crop response and facility decision rules.

sections.title: Separate identification from treatment authorization
sections.body: Identification confidence and intervention authority are different controls. Management options and pesticide registrations change with crop, jurisdiction, production setting and label; use the current authorized facility procedure and applicable label rather than a static course recipe.

workedExamples: Ten aphids found on one heavily sampled plant and ten aphids spread across many sampled plants are not equivalent evidence of incidence or distribution.
Honeydew and aphid cast skins on stems can support an aphid workup when plant yellowing alone would remain nonspecific.
commonMistakes: Using an unsupported universal aphid threshold for hemp or cannabis.
Calling honeydew alone proof of cannabis aphid without finding the causal organism.
Treating a course discussion of management categories as authorization to select or apply a pesticide.
content.practicalApplication: Create an aphid scouting record that includes sampled units, plant location, life stages observed, honeydew or cast-skin evidence, affected crop stage, spatial distribution and follow-up plan. State clearly whether identity is suspected, probable or confirmed.
content.summary: Cannabis aphid diagnosis combines direct organism evidence with distribution and crop response. Thresholds and treatment authority must remain tied to validated local rules rather than invented universal numbers.
